standard_prerequisites.name: A module annihilated by a power of the ideal is a module over the quotient, and tensoring it over the quotient against the base changed quotient gives back the module when the quotients agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Establishes the case of a module annihilated by a fixed power through the displayed chain of isomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: A power torsion module is the union of the submodules annihilated by the successive powers of the ideal, and tensor products commute with direct limits
standard_prerequisites.use: Passes from the fixed powers to an arbitrary power torsion module.

standard_prerequisites.name: The completion of the ring with respect to a finitely generated ideal is a special case of the base change setting, namely the base change along the completion map
standard_prerequisites.use: Deduces the final assertion of the statement from the general one.

core_obligations: Prove the case of a module annihilated by a fixed power of the ideal: display the chain of isomorphisms identifying its base change with the tensor product over the quotient against the base changed quotient, then with the module over the quotient, and finally with the module itself, using that the quotients agree (proof lines 24185-24190).

Pass to an arbitrary power torsion module by writing it as the union of the submodules annihilated by the successive powers and using that tensor products commute with direct limits, which gives the general isomorphism (proof lines 24190-24196).

Deduce the final assertion: for a finitely generated ideal the completion map is an instance of the setting, so the general statement applies and the power torsion module is unchanged by tensoring with the completion (proof lines 24196-24198).
proof_roadmap: Fixed power case by the displayed chain of identifications over the quotient (proof lines 24185-24190).
General case by the union description and commutation of tensor products with limits (proof lines 24190-24196).
Completion case as a special case of the general statement (proof lines 24196-24198).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that if a ring map induces isomorphisms on the quotients by all powers of an ideal, then the base change of any power torsion module along that map is an isomorphism, and identifies the case of the completion of a finitely generated ideal as a special case (statement lines 24172-24183). The proof is a two-stage computation: for a module annihilated by a fixed power the base change is identified with the tensor product over the quotient against the base changed quotient and hence with the module itself, and an arbitrary power torsion module is written as the union of those submodules so that the statement follows from commutation of the tensor product with direct limits (proof lines 24185-24198). The identification over the quotient is what makes the fixed power case immediate. The counted statement contains the author's reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so its citation is discarded and no bibliography is needed.
